title: Microbial Profiling of Low-Biomass Upper Respiratory Tract Samples
author: Odendaal, Chu, et al.
materials: Phusion Hot Start II high-fidelity DNA polymerase kit

This step involves isolating DNA from URT samples using mechanical and chemical cell lysis methods. The goal is to obtain high-quality DNA for downstream analysis (Figures 1 and 2).CRITICAL: To prevent contamination with unintended DNA, ensure a clean working environment by wearing gloves and thoroughly cleaning all surfaces and equipment with Actisan chloride (1 tablet per 1 L water; 0.15% Chloride w/v) / 70% ethanol v/v. Organize the workspace with only the necessary equipment. Use fresh buffers for each experiment, aliquoting them into single-use portions (one aliquot per extraction set) to prevent cross-contamination. Utilize sterile Eppendorf tubes and work in a fume hood that has been cleaned with chloride/ethanol. Always include one negative control sample per 24 samples to monitor for contamination.Note: It takes approximately 6 h to extract DNA from 48 samples. Make use of three different laboratory spaces (e.g., a reagent prep lab for reagent preparation, a DNA extraction lab for DNA extraction, and a third space for amplicon generation).1.Reagent preparation in a dedicated reagent prep lab.CRITICAL: DNA, RNA, amplicons, microbial agents or patient samples are not permitted in the reagent prep lab. Only enter this lab when you have not been in laboratory spaces where microbiological or patient material was handled beforehand. It is highly recommended to schedule work in the reagent prep lab at the beginning of the day. The equipment (pipettes, vortex etc.), consumables (tubes, tips, etc.) and lab coat should not be used/worn outside of the reagent prep lab (Figure 1). Prepare single use aliquots from all your reagents: binding buffer, lysis buffer and zirconium beads, wash buffers, magnetic beads, water and elution buffer. For example, prepare aliquots with enough volume for processing 24 samples at a time. Each aliquot of reagents must be clearly labeled with the following details: reagent name, LOT/batch number, aliquoting date and expiration date. Utilize safe-lock Eppendorf tubes for smaller volume reagents and sterile Falcon tubes for larger volumes.a.Dispense 600 μL of 0.1 mm zirconium beads into a screw cap tube (1.5 mL) containing approximately 300 μL of lysis buffer.i.Add additional lysis buffer if needed (see table at step 2.d) and place the tubes in a rack.b.Prepare negative control tubes by adding 200 μL of lysis buffer into a 1.5 mL screw cap tube.Note: Per 48 samples, it is advised to include two negative controls (blanks) and one positive control containing cells (ZymoBIOMICS microbial community standard).c.Prepare 2 mL tubes containing magnetic bead solution in binding buffer for the second part of the extraction.i.Vortex the magnetic beads thoroughly.ii.Add 10 μL of magnetic beads followed by 1300 μL of binding buffer into a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.Note: Cap the tubes immediately after each magnetic bead addition and avoid contact between gloves and the inside or rim of each tube. Vortex the stock tube every 12 sample tubes to keep the beads well-mixed and evenly distributed.2.Sample set-up in the DNA extraction lab.a.Clean the fume hood, materials and equipment (e.g., pipettes, Eppendorf racks, centrifuges, vortex) using 0.15% chloride w/v, followed by 70% ethanol v/v.i.Prepare separate waste bags in the fume hood (two) for phenol and (one) for biological/other waste, in accordance to your laboratory disposal guidelines.Note: Collect mixed phenol waste inside the working cabinet or fume hood to minimize exposure.b.Retrieve samples from the −80°C freezer and thaw them on ice.c.Label new 1.5 mL screw cap tubes with sample numbers on top. Additionally, label the 2 mL Eppendorf tubes filled with magnetic beads and binding buffer with sample numbers on both the top and side of the tubes.Note: These new caps will replace the old caps after step 2.d.Note: A minimum of four samples is necessary to balance the Beadbeater. Pipette the phenol from the bottom layer (beneath the buffer layer).ii.Mix samples by gentle vortex or pipetting up and down (1000 μL pipette with filter tips) before adding it to the tubes with the zirconium beads-lysis buffer-phenol mixture. This step includes assessing the concentration of MiSeq PCR products with PicoGreen, followed by pooling them into a amplicon library. The pooled amplicon libraries are then purified using AMPure XP reagent (bead-based), and their concentration is measured with KAPA qPCR. These procedures are crucial in preparing the samples prior to sequencing (Figure 3).12.Determine the concentration of MiSeq PCR products using PicoGreen.a.Use the setup in worksheet “Run_PCR_plate_X” in Table S1.b.Paste the fluorescence data from all plates into the appropriate cells, and generate the standard curve in worksheet “Plate setup & raw data” in Table S1.c.Perform a quality check to confirm that MiSeq PCR amplicon measurements are within the required range for downstream applications.i.Ensure that the R2 value of the standard curve is at least 0.98.ii.Confirm that the graph is linear and follows the equation Y = aX + b. Fill in the Y and X according to the graph in worksheet “SETUP_CALCULATION” in Table S1.iii.Verify that the amplicon readings fall within the range of the standard curve.iv.If any amplicon reading exceed the highest value on the standard curve, dilute those amplicons, re-measure, and adjust the final concentration by considering the dilution factor.v.Ensure that all amplicons have concentrations above 10 ng/μL, which is required for the final pool. If not, repeat the MiSeq PCR for those amplicons in a lower dilution. See worksheet “SETUP_CALCULATION” in Table S1.Note: If the MiSeq PCR amplicon is undiluted and contains less than 10 ng/μL, repeat the MiSeq PCR amplification to rule out errors. If sufficient material remains, repeat the DNA extraction. Otherwise, the sample will be considered a dropout. To improve DNA yield, consider performing double DNA extractions (see problem 1).Note: Negative PCR controls should have concentrations below 8 ng/μL. Negative DNA controls typically range between 6–15 ng/μL, but concentrations below 10 ng/μL are generally considered low. Higher concentrations as determined by the qPCR results may indicate contamination and indicate that the run should be evaluated carefully (see problem 2).d.Use the gel electrophoresis to verify the amplicon size, and ensure that the band size and thickness on the gel correspond to the expected amplification and PicoGreen data.Note: The product size of the gel electrophoresis should be approximately 400 base pairs (bp) for the V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene. Print the gel image and rename the lanes accordingly.e.After determining the concentration with PicoGreen, pool either 100 or 150 ng of each MiSeq PCR amplicon.i.Refer to the “List_view_POOL” worksheet in Table S1 for the sample volumes needed to create an equimolar pool.Note: The choice between 100 and 150 ng depends on the sample concentrations: for highly concentrated samples requiring small volumes, pooling at 150 ng helps minimize pipetting errors. Each pool will use a single chosen concentration. Worksheet “Submission_form” in Table S1 contains an overview of the results and measurements.13.AMPure bead purification.a.Perform AMPure bead purification twice on the pooled amplicon library using a ratio of 0.9 (pool:AMPure) according to the standard protocol of the supplier.10i.Use 500 μL of the pooled amplicon library and add this to the AMPure beads.ii.Perform washing steps with 70% Ethanol v/v and elute in 100 μL of elution buffer (QIAGEN).iii.Repeat the purification steps with the 100 μL eluate as input, and finish with 35 μL of eluate.iv.Prepare a 10x dilution of this eluate and test it using the KAPA qPCR.Note: We perform the purification twice to ensure thorough removal of impurities and to maximize the recovery of target DNA fragments.1014.Library concentration measurement with KAPA library quantification kit (Illumina platforms) and qPCR:a.Use the KAPA qPCR template for experimental design according to worksheet “KAPA-1 PCR setup” in Table S2.b.Dilute the amplicon library 100,000x and measure in triplicate.c.Include controls and the standard curve provided in the kit.d.Thaw reagents on ice and minimize their time at room temperature (19°C–21°C).e.Prepare the mix according to the instructions in worksheet “KAPA-1 PCR setup” in Table S2.f.Run the KAPA qPCR using the program specified in the same worksheet.g.Analyze results using worksheet “KAPA-1 analysis” in Table S2 (see problem 3).h.Store the library at −20°C.i.Dilute the library to 8 nM in elution buffer (QIAGEN) according to worksheet “load and run Miseq” in Table S2, measure again using KAPA qPCR worksheet “KAPA-2 PCR setup” and “KAPA-2 analysis”. Store at +4°C until the MiSeq run.Figure 3Schematic overview of the library purification and sequencing process

steps.title: Prepare reagents in dedicated lab
steps.instruction: In a reagent‑prep laboratory (no DNA, RNA, amplicons, microbial agents or patient material) aliquot all reagents for 24 samples: binding buffer, lysis buffer, 0.1 mm zirconium beads, wash buffers, magnetic beads, water and elution buffer. Label each aliquot with reagent name, LOT/batch, aliquoting date and expiration. Use safe‑lock Eppendorf tubes for small volumes and sterile Falcon tubes for larger volumes. Prepare 600 µL of 0.1 mm zirconium beads in a 1.5 mL screw‑cap tube and add ~300 µL lysis buffer (add extra lysis buffer later if required, see step 4). Prepare negative‑control tubes with 200 µL lysis buffer. For the magnetic‑bead stock, vortex beads thoroughly, then add 10 µL magnetic beads plus 1300 µL binding buffer into a 2 mL Eppendorf tube; cap immediately and vortex the stock tube after every 12 sample tubes.

steps.title: Clean extraction hood and set waste
steps.instruction: Clean the fume hood, pipettes, racks, centrifuge and vortex with 0.15 % Actisan chloride solution (1 tablet per 1 L water) followed by 70 % ethanol (v/v). Prepare two phenol waste bags and one biological/other waste bag inside the hood according to disposal guidelines. Collect mixed phenol waste inside the cabinet to minimise exposure.

steps.title: Thaw and label samples
steps.instruction: Retrieve URT samples (saliva, oropharynx, nasopharynx) from the –80 °C freezer and thaw on ice. Label new 1.5 mL screw‑cap tubes with sample numbers on the top; also label the 2 mL magnetic‑bead tubes on top and side. A minimum of four samples is required to balance the Beadbeater; ensure labels are placed before bead beating because the process can erase them.

steps.title: Add phenol to lysed samples
steps.instruction: To each 650 µL of 0.1 mm zirconium beads in lysis buffer (in the 1.5 mL tubes) add 550 µL phenol (pH 8.0 with Tris) using the same pipette tip for all tubes. Do not shake the phenol bottle; pipette from the bottom layer beneath the buffer. Mix gently by vortexing or pipetting up‑and‑down with a 1000 µL filter tip. Input volumes per sample type: Nasopharynx 200 µL (output 35–50 µL), Oropharynx 200 µL (output 50 µL), Saliva 50 µL (add 150 µL extra lysis buffer at step 1a‑i).

steps.title: Bead beat and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in the Beadbeater, secure the lock, and bead‑beat for 2 min at level 5 (≈3500 strokes/min). Cool on ice 2 min, repeat bead‑beating for another 2 min, then cool on ice 2 min again. Clean the Beadbeater with 70 % ethanol after use. Centrifuge the tubes at 4500 × g for 10 min at room temperature (19 °C–21 °C) in a rack (not on ice).

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Transfer the upper clear supernatant (≈±700 µL) to the corresponding 2 mL tube containing magnetic beads and binding buffer. Vortex briefly to mix. Use a fresh tip for any remaining sample. This step is critical for low‑DNA samples (<0.5 ng/µL in 1 mL).

steps.title: Incubate binding and magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes for ≥30 min at 900 rpm in a Thermoshaker HLC at room temperature (19 °C–21 °C). Disinfect the magnetic separator rack with 70 % ethanol. Spin down 10 s at 4500 × g, place tubes on the magnet for 1 min, then discard the supernatant into the phenol waste bag. The DNA is now bound to the beads.

steps.title: Wash beads with Wash Buffer 1
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL Wash Buffer 1 to each tube, vortex a few seconds, incubate 5 min at room temperature (19 °C–21 °C) in the Thermoshaker HLC, centrifuge 10 s at 4500 × g, place on magnet 1 min, and discard the supernatant into a non‑phenol waste bag using a 1000 µL tip. The supernatant should be phenol‑free.

steps.title: Wash beads with Wash Buffer 2
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL Wash Buffer 2, vortex briefly, incubate 5 min at room temperature (19 °C–21 °C) in the Thermoshaker HLC, centrifuge 10 s at 4500 × g, magnet 1 min. Pre‑heat the shaking heat block to 55 °C. Remove the supernatant carefully, tapping the magnet on the bench and using a 200 µL tip to eliminate residual droplets.

steps.title: Dry magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a Thermoshaker HLC at 55 °C for 15–20 min in the fume hood (no shaking). Do not exceed 25 min. Label new 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind DNA Eppendorf tubes for the upcoming eluate.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried beads in 50 µL elution buffer (LGC; volume may be adjusted if needed). Vortex a few seconds, incubate ≥15 min at 55 °C while shaking at 900 rpm, centrifuge 10 s at 4500 × g, magnet 1 min, then pipette the supernatant into the pre‑labeled Lo‑Bind DNA tubes. Store the eluate at –20 °C.

steps.title: Quantify amplicons with PicoGreen
steps.instruction: Using the worksheet “Run_PCR_plate_X” (Table S1), measure fluorescence of each MiSeq PCR product with PicoGreen. Paste data into “Plate setup & raw data” (Table S1) and generate a standard curve in “SETUP_CALCULATION”. Ensure R² ≥ 0.98, linear Y = aX + b, and that all amplicon readings fall within the curve range. Dilute and re‑measure any sample above the highest standard. All amplicons must be ≥10 ng/µL; otherwise repeat the MiSeq PCR (or DNA extraction, possibly a double extraction). Negative PCR controls must be <8 ng/µL; negative DNA controls typically 6–15 ng/µL (values <10 ng/µL are low and may indicate contamination).

steps.title: Verify amplicon size by gel
steps.instruction: Run the PCR products on an agarose gel and confirm a band of ~400 bp (V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene). Print the gel image and rename lanes according to sample IDs.

steps.title: Pool amplicons to target ng
steps.instruction: Pool either 100 ng or 150 ng of each amplicon to create an equimolar library (choose 150 ng for highly concentrated samples to reduce pipetting error). Use the “List_view_POOL” worksheet (Table S1) for the exact volumes. Record the pool composition in the “Submission_form” worksheet (Table S1).

steps.title: AMPure bead purification (first round)
steps.instruction: Add AMPure XP beads to the pooled library at a 0.9 : 1 (pool : AMPure) ratio: mix 500 µL pooled library with the calculated volume of beads. Perform the standard AMPure wash with 70 % ethanol, then elute in 100 µL QIAGEN elution buffer.

steps.title: AMPure bead purification (second round)
steps.instruction: Repeat the AMPure purification using the 100 µL eluate as input. After washing, elute in 35 µL elution buffer. Prepare a 10× dilution of this final eluate for KAPA qPCR.

steps.title: Prepare 10× dilution for KAPA qPCR
steps.instruction: Dilute the 35 µL eluate ten‑fold with nuclease‑free water to generate a sample for the KAPA library quantification assay.

steps.title: KAPA library quantification qPCR
steps.instruction: Follow the “KAPA‑1 PCR setup” worksheet (Table S2). Dilute the library 100 000‑fold and run each sample in triplicate together with the kit’s standards and controls. Keep reagents on ice, thaw only when needed, and keep them at 19 °C–21 °C for the shortest possible time. Prepare the reaction mix as described, run the program specified in the worksheet, and analyse results in “KAPA‑1 analysis”. Store the quantified library at –20 °C.

steps.title: Dilute library to 8 nM and store
steps.instruction: Dilute the library to a final concentration of 8 nM in QIAGEN elution buffer according to the “load and run Miseq” worksheet (Table S2). Verify the concentration with a second KAPA qPCR using the “KAPA‑2” worksheets. Store the 8 nM library at +4 °C until MiSeq sequencing.

steps.title: FastQC quality check of sequencing data
steps.instruction: After MiSeq run, run FastQC on the raw FASTQ files to assess read quality, per‑base quality, GC content, and adapter contamination.

steps.title: Demultiplex and generate ASV table
steps.instruction: Demultiplex reads and process them with the DADA2 pipeline (v1.9 or later) using the latest SILVA taxonomic training set. Export the resulting amplicon sequence variant (ASV) count table.

steps.title: Remove unwanted taxa and rename ASVs
steps.instruction: From the ASV table, remove any taxa assigned to ‘Mitochondria’, ‘Chloroplast’, ‘Archaea’, or ‘Eukaryota’. Rename each ASV with its lowest known taxonomic rank followed by its relative‑abundance rank in brackets (e.g., Streptococcus [1]).

steps.title: Identify contaminants with decontam
steps.instruction: Run the R package ‘decontam’ using the ‘combined’ method (prevalence + frequency) on the dataset together with negative‑control samples to flag contaminant ASVs (e.g., Comamonadaceae, Ralstonia, Thermus, Caulobacter). Remove these contaminants from the table.

steps.title: Generate rarefaction curves and filter samples
steps.instruction: Create rarefaction curves for each sample to determine the sequencing depth at which curves plateau. Exclude any sample whose read count falls below the plateau threshold before downstream analysis.

steps.title: Calculate alpha diversity metrics
steps.instruction: Using the ‘phyloseq’ and ‘microbiome’ R packages, compute alpha‑diversity indices such as observed species and Shannon index. Normalize counts for sequencing depth and visualise results with boxplots (median, IQR, whiskers as 1.5 × IQR).

steps.title: Perform beta diversity and PERMANOVA
steps.instruction: Calculate beta‑diversity distances (e.g., Bray‑Curtis) and visualise with Principal Coordinates Analysis (PCoA) or NMDS. Test group differences with PERMANOVA using the ‘vegan’ package.

steps.title: Cluster samples and assess significance
steps.instruction: Generate hierarchical clusters (complete or average linkage) based on Bray‑Curtis distances. Determine the optimal number of clusters with Calinski‑Harabasz and Silhouette indices. Visualise clusters with mosaic plots and test associations with logistic regression.

steps.title: Differential abundance analysis
steps.instruction: Identify taxa that differ between experimental groups using ‘MaAsLin2’ or ‘ANCOM‑BC2’. Report significant ASVs/taxa with appropriate effect sizes and p‑values.
